qs.q: A patient presents with keratitis, conjunctivitis, and iritis following a shingles outbreak. Which nerve involvement is likely responsible for these symptoms?
o: Involvement of the thoracic dorsal root ganglion
qs.e: Trigeminal nerve involvement in zoster can lead to ocular complications like keratitis, conjunctivitis, and iritis. Sacral nerves are involved in genital herpes, and facial nerve involvement causes Bell's palsy.
qs.s: Herpesviruses: HSV-1, HSV-2, VZV, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Tx: MCQs

qs.q: Which of the following agents is recommended for the treatment of Acanthamoeba Keratitis?
o: Topical PHMB or chlorhexidine eye drops
qs.e: Keratitis caused by Acanthamoeba is usually treated with topical agents such as PHMB or chlorhexidine. Amphotericin B is primarily reserved for systemic or central nervous system infections like GAE and PAM.

qs.q: Which statement regarding aspergillosis is correct? Aspergillus causes a wide range of local infections (otomycosis, keratitis, onychomycosis, sinusitis) beyond invasive pulmonary disease; blood cultures are usually negative even in invasive disease, so c is false. ---
o: Clinical manifestations include local infections of the ear and sinuses
Bone marrow transplant recipients are not at risk for invasive disease
Patients on parenteral corticosteroids are not at risk for invasive disease
Pulmonary aspergillosis is frequently diagnosed by culturing blood samples
Patients with allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis rarely have eosinophilia
qs.e: Aspergillus species frequently cause localized infections involving the ear, cornea, nails, and sinuses in addition to pulmonary manifestations.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Q&A: Fungal Pathogens, Drugs, & Diseases
